## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization over per-particle components can approach the streaming ceiling on low-churn workloads, with a host-scan reduction merge handling respawn.

## Cache saturation
All measured points start at N=4000, already past the L1d spill at N≈949, so the L1-resident regime is unobserved. At q=0.01, cost FALLS from 10.009 ns/p (N=4000) to 8.226 (N=16000) — overhead amortization at small N — then stays FLAT through the L2→DRAM spill at N≈60787: 8.226 ns/p at N=16000 (L2-resident) versus 8.078 at N=65000 (just spilled) shows no knee, and the curve holds 7.907–8.058 ns/p out to N=4M. Raising the death rate lifts the floor without reshaping the N-curve: q=0.05 plateaus near 8.3–8.9 ns/p, q=0.25 near 10.1–10.2 ns/p, each with the same small-N amortization and no spill knee. The L2→DRAM transition is invisible because per-particle working-set traffic (69 bytes) is too small relative to compute to expose a bandwidth wall.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved is 8.73 GB/s at N=262000, q=0.01 — 34.6% of the 25.22 GB/s streaming ceiling. The cell is overhead-bound, not bandwidth-bound: even at the largest N and lowest churn it never crosses 35% of ceiling. Bandwidth is stable across N within each death rate (8.5–8.7 GB/s for q=0.01 at N≥16000), confirming the bottleneck is per-particle compute overhead, not memory throughput. Death rate drives the transition: q=0.05 holds 7.7–8.3 GB/s but q=0.25 collapses to 6.74–6.83 GB/s, a 23% drop attributable to the branchy respawn path (35 `bl` calls to `_layouts.L1.data.Data.spawn`) whose cost rises with churn and dominates by q=0.25.

## Assembly
The compiler vectorized across the components of a single particle, not across particles. The loop body (stride 0x44=68 bytes) loads one particle via `ldr q16, [x11]`, `ldr d17, [x11, #0x10]`, and an indexed gather `ld1.s {v17}[1], [x12]` to pull a component at offset 0x14, then rearranges with `ext.16b v18, v16, v17, #0xc` before `fmul.4s v7, v18, v3` and `fadd.4s v7, v16, v7`. This component-wise packing explains the low bandwidth: each iteration touches a 68-byte struct spanning cache-line boundaries, and the indexed `ld1.s` insert prevents contiguous streaming. The mask write `strb w11, [x10], #0x1` is a byte-granular store to a separate array, adding a non-coalesced write per particle. The respawn path is fully scalar — `ldrb`/`cbz`/`bl` chains checking each mask byte individually — which is why high death rates degrade performance without changing the N-shape.

## Verdict
Refuted — the cell never exceeds 8.73 GB/s (34.6% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling) at q=0.01, N=262000, because component-wise vectorization within a stride-68 struct with an indexed `ld1.s` gather cannot stream, and the byte-granular mask store adds non-coalesced traffic. At q=0.25 the branchy respawn path (35 `bl` calls) further collapses bandwidth to 6.74 GB/s (27% of ceiling). The hypothesis that auto-vectorization approaches the streaming ceiling does not hold in any measured regime.
